facts.fact: The museum opened in Senkō-ji Park in Onomichi in 1980.
facts.quote: Onomichi City Museum of Art (尾道市立美術館, Onomichi shiritsu bijutsukan) opened in Senkō-ji Park in Onomichi, Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan, in 1980.

facts.fact: It reopened in 2003 to a design by Tadao Ando.
facts.quote: The Museum reopened to a design by Tadao Ando in 2003.

facts.fact: The collection includes works by artists connected to the city, plus foreign artists such as Georges Rouault.
facts.quote: The museum contains artworks by artists connected to the city, such as Guilin-in Hirata and Wasaku Kobayashi, as well as artworks by well known foreign artists such as French painter Georges Rouault.

facts.fact: It is a roughly 20-minute walk from Onomichi station.
facts.quote: The Museum is located in Senkō-ji Park, roughly 20 minutes walk from Onomichi station.

facts.fact: Hochhaus Neue Donau, also called the Seidler Tower, is a residential skyscraper in Vienna's Donau City district.
facts.quote: Hochhaus Neue Donau also known as the Seidler Tower is a residential skyscraper in the Donau City district of Vienna, Austria.

facts.fact: It was built between 1999 and 2001 and stands 150 m tall with 34 floors.
facts.quote: Built between 1999 and 2001, the tower stands at 150 m (490 ft) tall with 34 floors

facts.fact: Its elongated triangular plan aims to maximize water views for every apartment.
facts.quote: The elongated triangular design of the 34-story tower is inspired by the goal of maximizing beautiful water views for every apartment.

facts.fact: The longer wing faces south toward the Danube and the shorter wing points east toward the Kaiserwasser and Alte Donau.
facts.quote: The longer wing is oriented southward toward the Danube, while the shorter wing points east, towards the Kaiserwasser and the Alte Donau.

facts.fact: The Austrian-Australian architect Harry Seidler designed it.
facts.quote: The building, designed by the Austrian-Australian architect Harry Seidler

facts.fact: The facade is white aluminum cassettes, segmented into four sections around a triangular centre.
facts.quote: The white aluminum cassette facade is segmented into four sections. These create a triangular center, which is surrounded by three wings.

facts.fact: Rental offices fill the lower floors, with apartments above and penthouses on the top floor.
facts.quote: The ground floor to the 8th floor mainly contains rental offices. Floors 8 to 15 are divided into two-to three-room apartments, above that there are one-to two-room apartments, and on the top floor there are penthouses.

facts.fact: Mimar Sinan built the mosque for the admiral Sinan Pasha, in Beşiktaş, Istanbul.
facts.quote: It was built by the Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan for the admiral Sinan Pasha.

facts.fact: Work began after Sinan Pasha died in 1554; the foundation inscription records completion in November/December 1555.
facts.quote: Sinan Pasha died in 1554 and work began after his death. The gilded Arabic foundation inscription above the arched gateway of the mosque records the completion date as November/December 1555.

facts.fact: The forecourt is surrounded on three sides by the madrasa.
facts.quote: The forecourt of the mosque is surrounded on three sides by the madrasa.

facts.fact: The mosque is built of alternating layers of ashlar and brick.
facts.quote: The mosque is constructed of alternating layers of ashlar and brick.

facts.fact: A 12.6 metre dome is supported on six arches with two free-standing hexagonal piers.
facts.quote: The 12.6 metres (41 ft) dome is supported on six arches with two free-standing hexagonal piers.

facts.fact: In 1749 the inner five-domed portico of the north side was incorporated into the prayer hall.
facts.quote: The north side of the mosque originally had a double portico but in 1749 the inner portico with five domes was incorporated into the prayer hall.

facts.fact: The design has been compared with the earlier Üç Şerefeli Mosque in Edirne, which also has a dome on six arches and two free-standing piers.
facts.quote: The design of the Sinan Pasha Mosque has been compared with the earlier Üç Şerefeli Mosque in Edirne which dates from 1437 to 1448. In both mosques a dome is supported on six arches with two free-standing piers.

facts.fact: The house museum in Oak Park, Illinois was built in 1889 by Frank Lloyd Wright, who lived there with his family for two decades and expanded it several times.
facts.quote: It was built in 1889 by the American architect Frank Lloyd Wright, who lived there with his family for two decades and expanded it multiple times, and consists of two interconnected structures.

facts.fact: The house to the south is Shingle or Queen Anne style, while the studio to the north is Prairie style.
facts.quote: The house to the south was designed in either the Shingle style or the Queen Anne style, while the studio to the north was designed in the Prairie style.

facts.fact: Wright added rooms in 1895 and built the studio annex in 1898, where he and his associates designed dozens of buildings.
facts.quote: Wright added rooms to the house in 1895, and he built the studio annex in 1898, where he and his associates designed dozens of buildings.

facts.fact: Wright experimented with architectural features and generally used functional rather than purely decorative details.
facts.quote: In designing the building, Wright often experimented with various architectural features, and he generally used details that were functional rather than purely decorative.

facts.fact: The facades use brick, stone, battens and shingles, and both wood-frame sections are arranged around central fireplaces.
facts.quote: The facades are made of brick, stone, battens, and shingles. Both sections of the building are wood-frame structures arranged around central fireplaces.

facts.fact: The studio has a reception hall, library, office and double-height drafting room.
facts.quote: The attached studio has a reception hall, library, office, and double-height drafting room on the same story.

facts.fact: Wright's firm designed many Prairie style buildings after the studio was completed.
facts.quote: Wright's firm designed Prairie style buildings en masse after the studio's completion, though sources disagree on how many buildings they designed.

facts.fact: The Frank Lloyd Wright Preservation Trust has restored it to its 1909 appearance, and it is a National Historic Landmark.
facts.quote: The museum is managed by the Frank Lloyd Wright Preservation Trust, which has restored the building to its appearance in 1909, the year Wright moved out. The building is listed on the National Register of Historic Places as a National Historic Landmark

facts.fact: The Waldspirale is a residential complex in Darmstadt whose name means forest spiral, reflecting its plan and green roof.
facts.quote: The name translates into English as forest spiral, reflecting both the general plan of the building and the fact that it has a green roof.

facts.fact: Friedensreich Hundertwasser designed it, Heinz M. Springmann planned and implemented it, and it was completed in 2000.
facts.quote: It was designed by Austrian artist Friedensreich Hundertwasser, planned and implemented by architect Heinz M. Springmann, and constructed by the Bauverein Darmstadt company. The building was completed in 2000.

facts.fact: It contains 105 apartments and a parking garage.
facts.quote: It contains 105 apartments and a parking garage.

facts.fact: The U-shaped building has a facade that does not follow a regular grid, with windows that appear to dance out of line.
facts.quote: Peculiarities of the U-shaped building are the unique facade, which does not follow a regular grid organization, and the windows, which appear as if they were "aus der Reihe tanzen" (dancing out of line)

facts.fact: A grass, shrub and tree-planted diagonal roof rises like a ramp along the U-form, reaching 12 floors at its highest.
facts.quote: The diagonal roof, planted with grass, shrubs, flowers and trees, rises like a ramp along the U-form. At its highest point, the building has 12 floors.

facts.fact: Over 1000 windows are all unique.
facts.quote: The windows of the Waldspirale, which number over 1000, are all unique: no two windows are the same.

facts.fact: Hundertwasser's style shows in the gilded onion domes, absence of straight lines, earth-tone painting and ceramic columns.
facts.quote: the gilded onion domes, the absence of straight lines and sharp corners, the multicoloured painting of the building in earth tones and the colourful ceramic columns.

facts.fact: MAAT is a Lisbon museum focused on art, architecture and technology.
facts.quote: MAAT is a cultural project for the city Lisbon that is focused on three areas - Art, Architecture, and Technology.

facts.fact: It sits on the River Tagus to the west of the city centre.
facts.quote: The €20m museum sits on the River Tagus (Rio Tejo) to the west of the city centre.

facts.fact: The new building links to the Tejo Power Station, a prominent example of early 20th-century industrial architecture.
facts.quote: It establishes a connection between the new building and the Tejo Power Station, one of Portugal's most prominent examples of industrial architecture from the first half of the 20th century

facts.fact: Amanda Levete Architects designed the museum.
facts.quote: The museum is designed by Amanda Levete Architects.

facts.fact: The programme opened on 30 June 2016, and the new building opened to the public on 5 October 2016.
facts.quote: MAAT's programme opened on 30 June 2016 with four exhibitions held in renovated spaces of the Tejo Power Station building. On 5 October of the same year, the new building opened to the public

facts.fact: The Hansahochhaus was Cologne's first skyscraper and one of the first in Germany.
facts.quote: When constructed in 1924-25 it was the city's first skyscraper, and one of the first skyscrapers in Germany.

facts.fact: Local architect Jacob Koerfer designed it as an Expressionist office building.
facts.quote: It was designed as an office building in the Expressionist style by the local architect, Jacob Koerfer.

facts.fact: It was constructed in just 135 working days.
facts.quote: It was constructed in just 135 working days

facts.fact: With 17 floors and 65 meters, it was briefly Europe's tallest building.
facts.quote: With 17 floors and a total height of 65 meters, for a brief period following its construction the Hansahochhaus was Europe's tallest building.

facts.fact: It is protected under historic monument legislation.
facts.quote: It is currently protected under historic monument legislation.

facts.fact: The Perelman Performing Arts Center, or PAC NYC, is a multi-space performing arts center at the northeast corner of the World Trade Center complex.
facts.quote: The Perelman Performing Arts Center, also known as 6 World Trade Center (6 WTC) and branded as PAC NYC, is a multi-space performing arts center at the northeast corner of the World Trade Center complex in Manhattan, New York City.

facts.fact: Gehry Partners and Snøhetta were the original designers, but those plans stalled and were scrapped.
facts.quote: Gehry Partners LLP and Snøhetta were selected as the original designers, but plans were repeatedly stalled and later scrapped.

facts.fact: The center opened on September 13, 2023.
facts.quote: The center, known during construction as the Ronald O. Perelman Performing Arts Center at the World Trade Center, opened on September 13, 2023.

facts.fact: The building measures 160 by 160 feet and 117 feet tall, resting on a black-granite pedestal.
facts.quote: The Performing Arts Center measures 160 by 160 feet (49 by 49 m) across and 117 feet (36 m) tall, resting upon a black-granite pedestal that measures 21 feet (6.4 m) tall.

facts.fact: The facade is 5,000 panels of veined Portuguese marble that turn amber at night.
facts.quote: The building's facade consists of 5,000 panels of veined Portuguese marble. The panels contain lozenge-shaped patterns and turn an amber color at night.

facts.fact: There are no windows on the facade, keeping theatergoers' buzz away from memorial visitors.
facts.quote: There are no windows on the facade; according to Ramus, this "keeps the buzz of theatergoers at a respectful distance from people who are paying tribute at the memorial, and vice versa".

facts.fact: Three theaters have walls that can rotate and expand to make extra space for a single theater.
facts.quote: All three theaters are designed so that the walls will be able to rotate and expand to provide extra space for a single theater if needed.

facts.fact: To reduce vibration from nearby subway lines, the theaters are separated by 1-foot-thick pads.
facts.quote: To reduce vibrations from nearby subway lines, the three theaters are separated from each other and from nearby structures by 1-foot-thick (0.30 m) pads.

facts.fact: Tournay Abbey is an active Benedictine monastery in Tournay, Hautes-Pyrénées.
facts.quote: Tournay Abbey (French: Abbaye Notre-Dame de Tournay) is an active Benedictine monastery in Tournay, Hautes-Pyrénées, France.

facts.fact: A priory was established on the site in the 11th century and became an abbey in the 17th century.
facts.quote: A priory was first established on the site in the 11th century, which became an abbey in the 17th century.

facts.fact: A new abbey was founded in the 1930s in Madiran and moved to Tournay in 1952, a year after a new monastery was built.
facts.quote: A new abbey was founded in the 1930s in Madiran and was transferred to Tournay in 1952, the year after construction of a new monastery.

facts.fact: The building was completed in 1958.
facts.quote: The building was completed in 1958.

facts.fact: It houses a community of about 20 monks.
facts.quote: The abbey remains active and houses a community of approximately 20 monks.
